title: iOS Metal Gaussian-splat render de-risk (depth sort + on-device 30 fps)
summary: Retire the #1 program risk: render a reconstructed Gaussian splat correctly, depth-sorted, at 30 fps on a physical iPhone in Unity 6 URP. Trainer-orthogonal — the failure is Unity's per-frame Metal depth sort (aras-p radix sort glitches on Metal, issue #226). Plan in design/proposals/ios-splat-render-v1.md: baseline aras-p (MIT) on desktop, then fix the Metal sort with a tile-local bitonic sort (msplat approach) or a native Metal plugin wrapping MetalSplatter (MIT); hold splats to ~1-2.5M via gsplat MCMC + SOG/.spz. Render-path-first (Owner decision, AUTH #030 spike).
deliverables: unity/ (splat render integration + iOS Metal sort fix or native plugin)

acceptance_tests.test: aras-p/UnityGaussianSplatting (MIT) is integrated in Unity 6 URP via GaussianSplatURPFeature (render graph, Compatibility Mode off) and renders a corpus splat correctly in the Editor/desktop as the baseline.

On a physical iPhone, splats render with correct back-to-front depth ordering (no glitching) using the chosen Metal sort fix — a tile-local bitonic sort (Option A) or a native Metal plugin wrapping MetalSplatter (Option B). This is the gate for 'solved'.

At a room splat budget (~1-2.5M, gsplat MCMC), sustained frame rate and package size are recorded against the 30 fps and <=150 MB targets, with SOG/.spz compression. Measurements are suggested evidence (SPEC §11), not a gate.
An LOD / chunked-streaming approach is specified (aras-p has none) so larger or multi-room scenes stay within budget on device.
The renderer loads splats only through signed, short-lived URLs (SECURITY_CHECKLIST §3.1), never a direct storage URL.

history.event: created by the Builder as the render-first spike track (the #1 program risk, orthogonal to the trainer). Plan in design/proposals/ios-splat-render-v1.md; complements M0-UNITY-02 (general renderer) and M1-CAPT-03 (produces the splat).

Builder drafted the implementation runbook (unity/docs/splat-render-integration.md): aras-p package wiring + URP feature, splat import + budget, and a Metal-safe sort-fix ladder — global bitonic sort (drop-in for aras-p's radix sort; reference compute kernel included) first, tile-local bitonic / MetalSplatter native plugin only if it misses 30 fps — plus the on-device test procedure. Editor/device implementation is the Operator's next step.

gj-operator: Tier B Metal-safe sort built (unity/Assets/GiganticJourneys/Splats/Sorting/). A wave-free flip/disperse bitonic compute sort (threadgroup-local stages, no padding buffer) plus the MetalSafeSplatSort component, which takes over the pinned aras-p package's sort buffers without modifying the package. Auto mode engages on Metal only, and SplatRenderSettingsApplier adds it to every tiered splat. Box evidence: 25/25 EditMode tests, including the GPU sort matching the CPU reference bit for bit on Vulkan (n up to 70 001); the package-binding guard runs in CI. AT-4 LOD/chunked-streaming spec written in qa/reports/M1-ios-splat-render.md. Still open: AT-2 (correct ordering on a physical iPhone, the gate) and AT-3 (fps at 1-2.5M splats) need the device via the internal-debug TestFlight build, which needs a splat in a build scene (M1-GAME-01). AT-5 (signed URLs) waits on the Supabase signed-URL endpoint. open -> in-progress. Delivered as direct commits to main (Operator precedent); the branch name is nominal.

Commits 1dee36e, 4dbe4ec, ca38c31, 2e479fc (PlayMode test isolation fix after unity-tests 37132813149 failed). Internal-debug TestFlight build 48 (run 37137079024, green, uploaded) carries the room. gj-operator: Owner device check of build 48 (iPhone 14): render and Tier B sort work (label 'Tier B'), but 20-23 fps (p99 frame 43-48 ms), heavy floaters/needle splats near the floor, and the capsule turned black among splats; he asked for a free camera angle. Fixes (commits bd469b4, 3d07bae): (1) black character root cause = the package composite divides by splat alpha, 0/0 = NaN where every splat is behind an opaque object, which blends to black on Metal; GJ alpha-safe composite shader (package unmodified). (2) Display prune tool (services/reconstruction/tools/prune_splat_ply.py, rules in splat_ops.DisplayPrune): 780,004 -> 400,000 splats (faint 138,764, giant 9,619, needle 14,269, out of bounds 7,636, isolated 19,610, then most-opaque budget). (3) Perf profile: render scale 0.7, SH order 1, Tier B sort at most every 2nd frame and only after 3 cm / 1.5 deg of camera motion, MSAA and HDR off on the room camera. (4) Touch orbit camera (drag outside stick/jump to orbit, pinch to zoom, gamepad right stick), on in MovementTest too; provisional numbers, movement.json unchanged. New package environments/_devtest/medieval-great-hall-winchester/splat-room-unity-v2-400k.tar.gz (15,675,479 bytes, sha256 64b182c8...). Internal-debug TestFlight build 50 (run 37167356135, uploaded 8:36 PM CT; release build 49 green). AT-2/AT-3 remain open pending the Owner's re-check.

gj-operator: Owner device check of internal-debug build 50 (iPhone 14, iOS 26.6.1; evidence qa/evidence/M1-UNITY-01/: his perf report + 3 screenshots). AT-2 PASS on device (Owner): Tier B Metal-safe sort orders the 400K-splat room correctly, no popping while orbiting or walking; the capsule now shades normally (alpha-safe composite fix confirmed). Device video not captured; the report and screenshots stand in. AT-3 recorded: fps p50 60.0 / avg 57.8, frame p50 16.7 ms / p99 33.4 ms over 60 s (3,470 frames), 400,000 splats, render scale 0.70, SH 1, package 15.7 MB (target 30 fps and <=150 MB met). Owner feedback: orbit camera great; room cleaner but still smeared near floor, columns and entrance, with white blown-out blobs and dark shapes where the capture never looked; Round Table end sharp. Report discrepancy: sort_every_nth_frame 1 although the room asked for 2 - the tier applier re-applied the High tier cadence (1) to the renderer after the Metal-safe sort parked the package sort, and the sort adopts the applier's value on the next camera; fixed by routing the room's SH order and cadence through SplatRenderSettingsApplier overrides, plus a per-frame-kind split of frame times (after sort / after label refresh / other) in the report to tell whether the p99 33 ms frames come from sort frames.

gj-operator: splat room v3 for the next internal-debug build. Retrained Winchester on Modal L40S with the quality recipe (30k iterations, antialiased rasterize, bilateral-grid per-image exposure compensation, scale regularisation; frames and COLMAP model reused): held-out LPIPS 0.278 -> 0.253 (PSNR 24.93 -> 23.70, penalised by the train-only exposure grid), $0.60; a pose-refinement variant ($0.68) was rejected (eval views offset). Pruned 828,710 -> 400,000 and compared on the box against v2 from the same views (sharper, fewer white floaters; out-of-coverage areas still poor) -> shipped as splat-room-unity-v3-400k.tar.gz (15,067,234 bytes, sha256 c9969c40...897e3c). Camera and play-area limits from the training-camera coverage (services/reconstruction/tools/room_limits.py, 3517ff8): walk x -2.26..2.39 / z -3.86..0.79 m, camera box walk+1 m, orbit pitch -10..22.6 deg, zoom 0.6..1.3, view yaw 4.4 +/- 45 deg, occluder walls on the thin x sides, camera pull-in and sphere-cast collision. Modal October spend after the retrain: $4.71 metered (under the $20/month cap). Generative repair of never-seen regions split out as research spike M1-PIPE-02.
